players.name: Malachi Toney
players.summary: Set Miami's single-game receptions record with 16 catches for 194 yards and three touchdowns in the 52–23 win over Pittsburgh on October 24.

players.name: Keyone Jenkins
players.summary: Passed for 293 yards and three touchdowns, added a rushing score and led UCF's 39–31 double-overtime upset of No. 2 BYU on October 24.

players.name: Devon Dampier
players.summary: Rushed for 150 yards and two touchdowns as unbeaten Utah rallied past No. 14 Houston 21–13 on October 24.

players.name: Drew Mestemaker
players.summary: Threw for 386 yards and four touchdowns in Oklahoma State's 57–24 win over Colorado, including a 34–0 second-half surge.

players.name: Jahiem White
players.summary: Ran for 174 yards and two touchdowns and added 58 receiving yards in North Texas' 49–39 win at Navy on October 24.

No. 1 Miami visits Chapel Hill after Malachi Toney's record-setting performance against Pittsburgh; ABC prime-time ACC matchup.

setup: No. 1 Miami brings a 7–0 record and an unbeaten ACC run to Chapel Hill after scoring 52 points against Pittsburgh. North Carolina is 4–3 following a 31–30 overtime loss to Syracuse, so this meeting puts the Hurricanes’ explosive passing offense against a Tar Heels team trying to regain its late-game composure.

things.title: Can UNC disrupt Mensah’s rhythm?
things.body: Miami quarterback Darian Mensah completed 31 of 37 passes for 387 yards and four touchdowns against Pittsburgh. UNC needs pressure and tighter coverage windows to prevent another game dictated by early, efficient Hurricane drives.

things.title: Keeping Malachi Toney from taking over
things.body: Toney caught a Miami single-game record 16 passes for 194 yards and three scores against Pittsburgh. North Carolina must tackle promptly underneath and avoid giving Miami's leading target room to turn ordinary completions into explosive gains.

things.title: North Carolina’s response after Syracuse
things.body: The Tar Heels lost 31–30 in overtime after giving up late scoring opportunities to Syracuse. Billy Edwards Jr. and the UNC offense need sustained possessions and cleaner finishing to keep their defense from facing Miami’s attack repeatedly on short rest.

breakdown.bottom_line: Miami’s high-efficiency passing game and North Carolina’s ability to sustain drives define this matchup. If the Tar Heels limit explosive catches and finish their own possessions, the game becomes a different test from the wide-open contest Miami played against Pittsburgh.
